notes: The page continues an equivalent condition on g: the author writes an existential relation with q,r in the starred hatted integer group and frames the equation. The marginal note recommends the inverse form sigma_infinity(g^{-1})=l_0^beta g l_1^gamma, says that passage to the abelian group gives beta=gamma (i.e. q=-r), and repeats the inverse form with beta on both generator factors.

In the main text the author replaces g by l_0^alpha g l_1^{-alpha}, writes the corresponding expression for sigma_infinity(g'), substitutes it into a relation with q',r', and gives an expanded and a simplified equality. He concludes that q,r depend on the outer automorphism defined by u, not on its representative in the normalizer of L_0. The cancelled phrase before de son représentant remains uncertain and has not been silently repaired.

For tau, the author uses g=l_1 and writes q=-1,r=1. The final paragraph says that for the discrete groups, besides the identical outer automorphism, there is only one other solution to the equations under the indicated generator and fundamental-relation requirements. An insertion supplies donc p=±1 et before que; its possible final closing curve is explicitly qualified after blind rereading. The final sentence continues beyond the sheet; no continuation from another scan was consulted.

The opening main-text parenthesis before Condition is not closed on this sheet, and the final en exigeant construction has no certain closing parenthesis; a small curve after the inserted et remains explicitly unresolved. These remain as written. There is no authorial date or explicit doubt phrase on this page. The handwritten page number is 9 at the lower left.

C's lower-case/upper-case distinction at the marginal initial and its added , que after abélien have been corrected from the ink. C's two indexed doubt marks are resolved on crop03. Its nested doubt inside the cancellation is retained. H's two note paragraphs are editorial and are excluded from the transcription. The long main word normalisateur crosses a manuscript line break; it is transcribed continuously.

No mathematical proof, formal computation, or independent algebra check was performed by this reader. Statements above describe the author's claims. Root reviewed the fourteen existing crops and concurred on the reported readings before this report was finalized; any separate root algebra check is not claimed here.

Main-reader local check of the marginal rewriting: put a=l₀, b=l₁ and s=σ∞, so s interchanges a and b. The displayed g b^q s(g)=a^r implies s(g)⁻¹=a^−r g b^q. In the abelianization write g=(A,B); the equation gives A+B=r and A+B+q=0, hence q=−r. Thus the marginal beta and gamma equal −r and q respectively, explaining the written β=γ. This algebraic check does not replace the direct reading of the signs.

Main-reader local check of representative invariance: if g′=a^α g b^−α, then s(g′)=b^α s(g)a^−α, and g′b^q s(g′)=a^α g b^q s(g)a^−α=a^α a^r a^−α=a^r. The same q and r therefore remain valid after the replacement shown. The discrete-group classification stated at the foot of the page was not independently proved here.

The clearly written star in q,r∈Ẑ* is retained. Taken literally, requiring both exponents to be units excludes g=1 with q=r=0, even though the following discrete discussion includes the identity. This is a tension in the stated condition, not a license to remove the star.

The blind audit confirms autom rather than action in both occurrences from the absence of an i dot and the low final om course. The first marginal inverse remains live. It adds ce as an alternative to the last cancelled word, and marks the colon-like points by the tau equality and the possible closing curve after the insertion as unresolved. The existing algebra checks concern the retained mathematical equality and do not settle these small pen marks.
